script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: friendship

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. SUBURBAN KITCHEN - MORNING

Mrs. HENRY (40s, warm, encouraging) pours a bowl of cereal for her son, LUCAS (9, energetic, curious).

MRS. HENRY
You have a big day ahead, Lucas. Don't forget about your school project.

LUCAS
(groans)
Mom, not this again. I've got it. I just need to find a friend to help me.

INT. LUCAS'S BEDROOM - DAY

Lucas sits on his bed, flipping through a school newsletter. He comes across an article about a new student, MAX (8, quiet, thoughtful), transferring to his school.

Lucas looks up from the paper with a determined expression.

LUCAS
(to himself)
Max. He could be the perfect friend for my project.

EXT. SCHOOL - DAY

Lucas waits at the bus stop. He spots Max getting off the bus, carrying a large stack of books.

LUCAS
(excitedly)
Hi, Max! I'm Lucas. We're in the same class. Need some help with a school project?

MAX
(surprised)
Hey, Lucas. Nice to meet you. No, I don't have any projects, but I'd be happy to help if I can.

INT. LUCAS'S LIVING ROOM - AFTERNOON

The two boys work together on their project, sharing ideas and laughter.

LUCAS
(grinning)
You know, Max, I've never really had a friend before. But with you, it feels like...it just feels right.

MAX
(smiling)
I feel the same way, Lucas. I'm glad we met.

INT. SCHOOL CAFETERIA - DAY

The boys proudly present their project to their class. They receive applause and admiration from their classmates.

LUCAS
(looking at Max)
Max, we did it!

MAX
(smiling)
We sure did, Lucas.

INT. SUBURBAN KITCHEN - EVENING

Mrs. Henry watches her son and his new friend as they chat animatedly at the kitchen table.

MRS. HENRY
(satisfied)
I'm so glad you found a friend, Lucas.

INT. LUCAS'S BEDROOM - NIGHT

Lucas gazes out the window at the stars, a smile on his face.

LUCAS
(whispering)
Max. You're the best friend I ever had.

FADE OUT.

THE END
